mainTopic: Which mourning practices of an אבל also apply to a מנודה and to a מצורע.
overview: The גמרא goes through the mourning practices of an אבל one at a time: haircuts, wrapping the head, תפילין, greeting people, learning Torah, laundering and tearing clothes. For each practice it first gives the source for the אבל, usually from what ה׳ told יחזקאל or the sons of אהרן. Then it asks whether the same rule applies to a מנודה and to a מצורע. A ברייתא forbids both of them to cut their hair or launder, and adds that בית דין places a stone on the coffin of a מנודה who dies in his ban. Several proofs about the מנודה are pushed away by אביי or others, and some questions end in תיקו. Still, a ברייתא shows that a מנודה may learn Torah, while a מוחרם may only learn alone. For the מצורע, פסוקים and ברייתות show that he wraps his head, may not greet, must tear his clothes, and may learn Torah. The amud ends by stating that an אבל must overturn his bed, with בר קפרא's teaching continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a banned person or a leper get a haircut?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether מנודין and מצורעין are allowed to cut their hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for people under a ban and for lepers when it comes to cutting their hair?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: may a מנודה or a מצורע get a haircut? This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is forbidden to cut his hair. The גמרא wants to know whether this mourning-style rule also covers a מנודה and a מצורע, who are also in a kind of 'distanced' state.

keyTerms.meaning: A person (people) placed under נידוי, a ban, by בית דין
A person (people) with צרעת, the biblical skin affliction

phrases.english: Those who are ostracized and lepers
what is their status regarding a haircut?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה and a מצורע are forbidden to cut their hair, the way an אבל is.

steps.title: A ברייתא says they may not cut hair or launder
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that מנודין and מצורעין may not cut their hair or launder their clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: People under a ban and lepers are forbidden to cut their hair and to launder their clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא: both a מנודה and a מצורע are forbidden to get a haircut. The ברייתא adds that they may not launder either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is a clear 'forbidden.' The ברייתא gives even more than the question asked, since it also forbids laundering. So on these two points a מנודה and a מצורע are treated like an אבל.
steps.whatToRemember: A מנודה and a מצורע may not cut their hair or launder, just like an אבל.

phrases.english: Come and hear: those who are ostracized and lepers
are forbidden to cut their hair and to launder.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מְנוּדִּין וּמְצוֹרָעִין אֲסוּרִין לְסַפֵּר וּלְכַבֵּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא rules that מנודין and מצורעין are forbidden both to cut their hair and to launder.

steps.title: When a banned person dies, the court stones his coffin
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: if a מנודה dies, בית דין stones his coffin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person under a ban dies, the court stones his coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא, which now adds another law: a מנודה who dies still has his ban marked, because בית דין 'stones' his coffin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death does not erase the ban. בית דין makes a public statement of disgrace even at the funeral. The next step explains what 'stoning' here really involves.

phrases.english: An ostracized person who died,
the court stones his coffin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנוּדֶּה שֶׁמֵּת, בֵּית דִּין סוֹקְלִין אֶת אֲרוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא with a further law about a מנודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a מנודה dies while still under his ban, בית דין 'stones' his coffin.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only one large stone, not a heap
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that the 'stoning' is one large stone placed on the coffin, not a heap like עכן's, to show that whoever dies in his ban gets this treatment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It does not mean they pile a heap of stones on him like the heap over עכן. Rather, the court sends people who place one large stone on his coffin. This teaches you that anyone who is banned and dies while still under the ban, the court stones his coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה explains how the 'stoning' is done: one big stone is placed on the coffin as a sign. Nobody builds a whole pile of rocks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might picture a real heap of stones like the one over עכן. רבי יהודה says it is only a symbolic act with one stone. The point is the lesson: a person who stays in his ban until death, without asking to be released, is publicly shown to have died in disgrace.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who took forbidden spoils from יריחו and was stoned
One who is placed under a ban

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody actually throws stones at the coffin here. According to רבי יהודה it is just one large stone set on top as a sign.
steps.whatToRemember: A מנודה who dies in his ban has a stone placed on his coffin. It is a sign of disgrace, not a real stoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not that they set up a heap of stones over him
like the heap of Achan,
rather, the court sends messengers
and they place a large stone on his coffin,
to teach you that anyone who is ostracized
and dies while still in his ostracism —
the court stones his coffin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא שֶׁיַּעֲמִידוּ עָלָיו גַּל אֲבָנִים כְּגַלּוֹ שֶׁל עָכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what 'stoning the coffin' in step 3 actually means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'stoning' is one large stone placed on the coffin, a symbolic act teaching that whoever dies in his ban is disgraced.

steps.title: A mourner must wrap his head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that an אבל is obligated in עטיפת הראש, covering the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is obligated to wrap his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new mourning practice and states the rule: an אבל must wrap his head. The proof comes in the next step, and the rule also sets up a question about the מנודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic in the list of mourning laws. Once the rule for an אבל is set, the גמרא can later ask whether a מנודה is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrapping or covering the head as a sign of mourning

phrases.english: A mourner is obligated in wrapping the head.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל must wrap his head.

steps.title: Proof from what ה׳ told יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ told יחזקאל, as a special exception, not to cover his lip in mourning. That shows everyone else must.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Merciful One told יחזקאל, 'And do not cover your upper lip,' we learn that everyone else is obligated to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the rule of step 5 from a פסוק in יחזקאל‎. ה׳ told יחזקאל to skip head-wrapping, so normally every mourner does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל was given an unusual command not to show the signs of mourning. A special command to skip something only makes sense if everyone else is normally required to do it. The proof works by inference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One': a name for ה׳, the Giver of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The obligation for an אבל to wrap his head is learned from the exception given to יחזקאל.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One said to Ezekiel:
"And do not cover your upper lip,"
it follows by inference that everyone else is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That an אבל must wrap his head.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 24:17: ה׳'s special command to יחזקאל not to cover his lip implies all other mourners must.

steps.title: Must a banned person wrap his head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה must also wrap his head like an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for a person under a ban regarding wrapping the head?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know an אבל wraps his head, the גמרא asks whether a מנודה does too. This sets up רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the haircut question. The גמרא checks each mourning practice to see if it carries over to a מנודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is it?': a question asking for the law

phrases.english: An ostracized person, what is his status regarding wrapping the head?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is obligated in עטיפת הראש like an אבל.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from the people fasting for rain
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא saying people wrap themselves and sit 'like מנודין and like אבלים,' which suggests a מנודה wraps his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: 'And they wrap themselves and sit like people under a ban and like mourners, until Heaven has mercy on them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to answer the question with a ברייתא. It describes people wrapping themselves 'like מנודין.' That suggests a מנודה really does wrap his head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares these people's wrapping to the behavior of a מנודה and an אבל. If a מנודה did not wrap his head, the comparison would not make sense. So רב יוסף concludes that a מנודה is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Until Heaven has mercy on them

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
and they wrap themselves and sit
phrases.notes: This quotes a ברייתא about people who fasted for rain and whose prayers were not answered.

phrases.english: like those who are ostracized and like mourners
until they are shown mercy from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, תָּא שְׁמַע: וְהֵן מִתְעַטְּפִין וְיוֹשְׁבִין כִּמְנוּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה must wrap his head.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing people who 'wrap themselves and sit like מנודין and like אבלים.'

steps.title: אביי: someone banned by Heaven may be different
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: the ברייתא may be talking about a person banned by Heaven, which is more serious than an ordinary מנודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe a person banned by Heaven is different, because that is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רב יוסף's proof. The people in the ברייתא are in a sense 'banned by Heaven,' and that may call for stricter behavior than an ordinary מנודה of בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not say a regular מנודה is exempt. He only says the ברייתא cannot prove he is obligated, because its case is more severe. So the question about a regular מנודה stays open at this point.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not ruling that a מנודה does not wrap his head. He is only showing that רב יוסף's source does not prove it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps one ostracized by Heaven is different, because it is more severe.
phrases.notes: 'Banned by Heaven' means the people whose fasts went unanswered, as if Heaven itself had distanced them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דִּלְמָא מְנוּדֶּה לַשָּׁמַיִם שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the law for an ordinary מנודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's case, someone 'banned by Heaven,' is more severe, so it cannot be applied to an ordinary מנודה of בית דין.

steps.title: Does a leper have to cover his head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע is obligated in עטיפת הראש, like an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מצורע regarding covering the head?
steps.whatsHappening: Having asked about a מנודה, the גמרא now asks the same question about a מצורע. Does he also have to cover his head?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that an אבל must cover his head. The גמרא is checking whether this mourning practice also applies to a מצורע, who is also in a kind of separated, mourning-like state.

keyTerms.meaning: A person afflicted with צָרַעַת (biblical skin disease)
What is the law? (a question formula)

phrases.english: A leper, what is [the law] regarding covering the head?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מנודה question (steps 7-9) to the same question about a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע must wrap his head like an אבל.

steps.title: The verse shows a leper must cover his head
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'and he shall cover his upper lip' proves that a מצורע must cover his head, and the גמרא accepts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And he shall cover his upper lip.' This implies he must cover his head. Learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק about the מצורע that tells him to cover his lip. Covering the lip means wrapping the head, so the question is settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same idea of covering the lip was used for the אבל in step 6. Here the תורה says it directly about the מצורע, so there is no doubt. The phrase שמע מינה closes the question with a firm yes.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from this we can infer
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And he shall cover his upper lip,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45. This פסוק is said about the מצורע himself.

phrases.english: which implies that he is obligated to wrap his head.
Learn from it [that this is so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, a מצורע must wrap his head, as the פסוק says 'he shall cover his upper lip.'

steps.title: A mourner may not put on תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states a new rule: an אבל is forbidden to put on תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is forbidden to put on תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new mourning law: an אבל does not put on תפילין. The source comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a second round of the same pattern used for עטיפת הראש. First a rule about the אבל, then a source, then questions about the מנודה and the מצורע.

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden to put on tefillin,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic (תפילין), parallel to step 5 (עטיפת הראש).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not put on תפילין.

steps.title: Proof from ה׳'s command to יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ told יחזקאל, while mourning, to wear his 'פאר' (תפילין). Since that was a special command, everyone else is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Merciful One told יחזקאל, 'Bind your headdress upon you,' we learn by implication that everyone else is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the rule. יחזקאל was specially told to wear תפילין while mourning, which shows that normally a mourner does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reasoning as step 6. If ה׳ had to tell יחזקאל specially to wear his פאר, then the normal rule for mourners must be the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One: a name for ה׳ as the giver of the תורה
Your glory / headdress: understood as תפילין

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One said to Ezekiel:
"Bind your headdress upon you,"
this implies that everyone else is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the rule of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That an אבל may not wear תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 24:17: the special command to יחזקאל implies the general prohibition.

steps.title: תפילין for a banned person: left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה may wear תפילין, and the question remains open (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: A person under a ban, what is the law regarding תפילין? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the תפילין rule for a mourner also applies to a מנודה. It finds no answer and leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallels step 7, where the same question was asked about עטיפת הראש. Here the גמרא does not even attempt a proof; it simply declares תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no.' It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: A banned person, what is [the law] regarding tefillin?
Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the new תפילין rule to the מנודה, as step 7 did for head-wrapping.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is forbidden to wear תפילין like an אבל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer; the question remains תיקו.

steps.title: Does a מצורע wear תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע may wear תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצורע, what is the law regarding תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the תפילין question about a מצורע. A proof attempt follows in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same order as before: first the מנודה, then the מצורע. For head-wrapping the מצורע had a clear פסוק; here the גמרא will have to search harder.

phrases.english: A leper, what is [the law] regarding tefillin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 10, now about תפילין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע is forbidden to wear תפילין.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר on the מצורע's clothes and head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר explains that the מצורע's clothes are torn and his 'פרוע' head means growing his hair long.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And the leper' includes the כהן גדול. 'His clothes shall be torn' means ripped. 'His head shall be פרוע' means growing the hair long. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. This part gives רבי אליעזר's view, which sets up רבי עקיבא's view in the next step, where the proof really lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, 'his head shall be פרוע' is about hair, not תפילין. The גמרא quotes him so we can see how רבי עקיבא reads the same words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And the leper (the word in the פסוק)

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And the leper"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: comes to include the High Priest.
"His clothes shall be torn"
means that they shall be ripped,
"and his head shall be פרוע"
פריעה means nothing other than growing the hair long,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for the question of step 15.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a מצורע may wear תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 13:45; this first part gives רבי אליעזר's view as background.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: 'his head' means something outside the body, maybe תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא compares the word 'shall be' by the head and by the clothes. Just as the clothes are outside the body, so too the head refers to something outside the body. The גמרא suggests this means תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'being' is said about the head, and 'being' is said about the garment. Just as the garment is something outside his body, so too the head means something outside his body. Isn't this about תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא links the head to the clothes and says the head law must be about something worn on the head, not the hair. The גמרא then suggests this must mean the מצורע may not wear תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothes are outside the body, so 'his head shall be פרוע' must also be about an object, not his hair. The most obvious object worn on the head is תפילין, so the מצורע must remove them. The phrase מאי לאו shows this is only a suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: The word 'shall be' (יהיה / יהיו) in the פסוק
Learning one place from another because they share a word

steps.confusionAlert: מאי לאו means 'isn't it so?' It offers a reading, but it is not yet a final conclusion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'Being' is stated regarding the head,
phrases.notes: 'His head shall be' (יהיה) and 'his clothes shall be' (יהיו) use the same verb.

phrases.english: and 'being' is stated regarding the garment.
Just as the 'being' stated regarding the garment
is something outside his body,
so too the 'being' regarding the head
is something outside his body.
Isn't it about tefillin?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: נֶאֶמְרָה הֲוָיָיה בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא; רבי עקיבא's reading supplies the actual proof attempt.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורע is forbidden to wear תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's גזרה שוה linking 'shall be' of the head to 'shall be' of the garment: both must refer to something outside the body.

steps.title: רב פפא: The head covering could be a cap or scarf, not תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the idea that רבי עקיבא's 'something outside the body on the head' must mean תפילין. It could mean an ordinary cap or scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: No. It could be talking about a cap or a scarf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down the proof from step 17. He says רבי עקיבא's 'thing on the head' could just be a regular cap or scarf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 tried to show that a מצורע may not wear תפילין, because רבי עקיבא spoke of something on the head that is outside the body. רב פפא points out that ordinary headwear also fits that description. So the ברייתא does not prove anything about תפילין, and the question about a מצורע and תפילין is left without a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: No; this proof does not work
A scarf or cloth wrapped around the head

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: No,
[it refers] to a cap and a scarf.
phrases.notes: He means the 'thing on the head' in רבי עקיבא's teaching could be regular headwear, so there's no proof about תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי עקיבא's teaching; it does not rule on whether a מצורע may wear תפילין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words 'outside the body on the head' fit a cap or scarf just as well as תפילין

steps.title: A mourner may not greet people
steps.stepSummary: An אבל may not greet others, learned from ה׳ telling יחזקאל to 'sigh in silence'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is forbidden to greet people, because ה׳ told יחזקאל: 'Sigh in silence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: an אבל may not greet people. It brings its source from what ה׳ told יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the תפילין discussion. Whatever יחזקאל was specially told about his mourning shows us what a regular אבל does. Since he was told to stay silent, a regular אבל may not greet people.

keyTerms.meaning: Greeting someone (literally, asking about their peace or welfare)

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden in greeting [people].
Since the Merciful One said to Ezekiel:
"Sigh in silence."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new mourning restriction, using the same יחזקאל-based method as step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not greet people

steps.title: May a person in נידוי greet people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה is also forbidden to greet people, like an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מנודה about greeting people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the greeting rule also applies to a מנודה. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question the גמרא asked in step 14 about תפילין. Now it asks it about greeting.

keyTerms.meaning: A person placed in נידוי, a kind of excommunication or ban

phrases.english: A person in nidui, what is [the law] regarding greeting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the greeting rule from step 19 to a new person
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is forbidden to greet people

steps.title: רב יוסף: People rebuked by Heaven may not greet each other
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: people who are 'rebuked by the Omnipresent' hold back from greeting each other. So a מנודה should not greet either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: And regarding greeting between a person and his friend, they act like people who are rebuked by the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to answer the question with a ברייתא. In it, people who are rebuked by Heaven may not greet each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'rebuked by the Omnipresent' is like being in נידוי from Heaven. If those people may not greet, a person in נידוי should not greet either.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said, come and hear:
And regarding greeting between a person and his friend,
[they are] like people who are rebuked by the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 20
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה may not greet people
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying that people rebuked by the Omnipresent do not greet each other

steps.title: אביי: Being rebuked by Heaven is more serious
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: a person under Heaven's ban is a more serious case, so we cannot learn from it to a regular מנודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe someone banned by Heaven is different, because that is more serious.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רב יוסף's proof. He says Heaven's ban is stricter than a ban from people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was about people rebuked by ה׳ Himself. A regular מנודה was banned by a בית דין, which may be less severe. So the extra strictness might apply only to Heaven's ban, and the question about a regular מנודה stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying a מנודה may greet people. He is only saying this proof does not show that he may not.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps one banned by Heaven is different, since it is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof in step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof; the question about a מנודה greeting people is left without an answer
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about a ban from Heaven, which is stricter than a regular ban from people

steps.title: May a מצורע greet people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע is forbidden to greet people.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מצורע about greeting people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same greeting question, now about a מצורע. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps comparing a מנודה and a מצורע to an אבל, just as it did with תפילין in steps 14 and 15. Now it checks whether the greeting rule applies to a מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin affliction

phrases.english: A leper, what is [the law] regarding greeting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same greeting question as step 20, about a different person
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע is forbidden to greet people

steps.title: A ברייתא: The מצורע keeps his lips closed and does not greet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains 'he shall cover his upper lip' to mean that the מצורע's lips stay closed. He is like a מנודה and an אבל, and may not greet people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And he shall cover his upper lip.' This means his lips should be stuck together. He should be like a מנודה and like an אבל, and he is forbidden to greet people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question directly. The פסוק about covering the lip teaches that a מצורע may not greet people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the מצורע covers his lip. The ברייתא reads this as keeping his mouth shut, meaning he does not talk and greet. It openly compares him to a מנודה and an אבל, and openly says he may not greet.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper lip or mustache area

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And he shall cover his upper lip" —
that his lips should be stuck to one another,
that he should be like one in nidui and like a mourner,
and he is forbidden in greeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורע may not greet people
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining the פסוק 'וְעַל שָׂפָם יַעְטֶה'

steps.title: Conclusion: A מצורע may not greet people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: a מצורע is forbidden to greet people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the ברייתא's proof and settles the question. A מצורע may not greet people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the מנודה questions, which stayed open, this proof is clear and nobody pushes back on it. The ברייתא says it directly, so the law is settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not greet people (from יחזקאל's 'sigh in silence'). For a מנודה, the proof was pushed away. A מצורע may not greet people, from the ברייתא on 'וְעַל שָׂפָם יַעְטֶה'.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מצורע is forbidden to greet people

steps.title: Using the מצורע ruling to settle the מנודה question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא about the מצורע also answers the earlier question about a מנודה greeting people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us settle from here the question about a מנודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a new proof. Since the ברייתא compared a מצורע to a מנודה, maybe it shows that a מנודה may not greet people either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the מצורע is 'like a מנודה and an אבל' and may not greet people. If the comparison means 'just as a מנודה may not greet,' then the open question about the מנודה is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us settle the question from this
A person placed under a ban (נידוי) by the court

phrases.english: Then let us settle from it the question about a מנודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the conclusion about the מצורע and tries to apply it back to the unanswered question about the מנודה.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה is forbidden to greet people
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא comparing the מצורע to a מנודה and an אבל

steps.title: The comparison is about other things, not greeting
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר פנחס says the ברייתא does not mean the מנודה is forbidden to greet. The מצורע is like a מנודה in other matters, and on top of that he may not greet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר פנחס said in the name of רב יוסף: Does the ברייתא say 'that he is forbidden' like them? It says 'that he should be like a מנודה and an אבל' in other matters, and he is also forbidden to greet people.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא's comparison to a מנודה covers other laws, and the ban on greeting is an extra rule for the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the greeting ban comes from the comparison to the מנודה. רב אחא בר פנחס reads it as two separate points: he is like a מנודה in other laws, and he also may not greet. So nothing is learned about whether a מנודה may greet.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach? (introduces a careful reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'like a מנודה' as proof that a מנודה may not greet. According to this answer, the greeting ban is stated as a separate rule for the מצורע. That does not prove a מנודה may greet either; the question about him is simply not settled.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר פִּנְחָס מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Pinchas said in the name of Rav Yosef:
Does it teach 'that he is forbidden' like them?
It teaches 'that he should be like a מנודה and like an אבל'
phrases.notes: Not every version has the word in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: in other matters,
and he is also forbidden to greet people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 26 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof about the מנודה; the ruling that a מצורע may not greet stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly linked the greeting ban to the comparison with a מנודה, when it is really a separate rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A מצורע may not greet people, but the question about a מנודה greeting stays open.

steps.title: An אבל may not learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: an אבל is forbidden to learn Torah, learned from what ה׳ told יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אבל is forbidden to learn Torah, since ה׳ told יחזקאל: 'Be silent.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic and states a rule: an אבל may not learn Torah. It also sets up the next question about a מנודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יחזקאל was told how to behave in mourning, he was told 'דֹּם', to stay silent. The גמרא takes this to include not speaking words of Torah.

phrases.english: An אבל is forbidden to learn words of Torah,
since the Merciful One said to יחזקאל: 'Be silent.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the greeting discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not learn Torah, based on 'דֹּם' said to יחזקאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known הלכה that an אבל does not learn Torah.

steps.title: May a מנודה learn Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה is also forbidden to learn Torah, like an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מנודה regarding learning Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that follows from the אבל rule. It is setting up a proof that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a מנודה shares many laws with an אבל, we might think he also may not learn Torah. The גמרא wants to know if that is true.

phrases.english: A מנודה, what is the law regarding words of Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the question raised by the אבל rule to the מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is forbidden to learn Torah like an אבל.

steps.title: A מנודה may learn and teach Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: a מנודה may teach Torah and be taught, and may be hired and hire others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear a ברייתא: A מנודה may teach and others may teach him; he may be hired and others may be hired by him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question with a ברייתא. A מנודה is allowed to learn and teach Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says openly that a מנודה teaches and is taught. So unlike an אבל, a מנודה may learn Torah. He may also work and hire workers.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches and others teach him
He is hired and others are hired by him

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
A מנודה may teach, and others may teach him,
he may be hired, and others may be hired by him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29 from a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מנודה may learn and teach Torah, and may work and hire workers.

steps.title: A מוחרם may only learn by himself
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: a מוחרם may not teach or be taught, nor be hired or hire. But he may learn alone so he does not forget, and run a small store to make a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מוחרם may not teach and others may not teach him; he may not be hired and others may not be hired by him. But he may learn by himself so he does not stop his learning, and he may make a small store for his living.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a stricter case, the מוחרם. He is cut off from learning with others and from working with others, with two small allowances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוחרם is under a harsher ban than a מנודה. He may not learn with others, but may learn alone so he will not forget his learning. He may also run a small store, enough to support himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A person under חרם, a harsher ban than נידוי

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not learn Torah. A מנודה may learn and teach. A מוחרם may not learn with others, but may learn alone and keep a small store to live.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מנודה and מוחרם. The מוחרם is the stricter ban, and that is why he is limited to learning alone.

phrases.aramaic: מוּחְרָם — לֹא שׁוֹנֶה וְלֹא שׁוֹנִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: A מוחרם may not teach, and others may not teach him,
he may not be hired, and others may not be hired by him.
But he may learn by himself,
so that he does not stop his learning,
and he may make himself a small store
for the sake of his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּחְרָם — לֹא שׁוֹנֶה וְלֹא שׁוֹנִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, setting the stricter מוחרם against the מנודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוחרם may not learn with others or do business with others, but may learn alone and run a small store for his living.
steps.whyThisMatters: The contrast shows how much harsher חרם is than נידוי: a מנודה may learn with others and do business freely, while a מוחרם is limited to learning alone and a tiny livelihood.

steps.title: רב explains the small store
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the 'small store' a מוחרם may run means selling water in the valley of ערבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: the small store means selling water in the valley of ערבות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains a word from the ברייתא in Step 31: what kind of 'small store' the מוחרם is allowed to run.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא let a מוחרם make a small living. רב gives an example: selling water in a dry place where nobody else has water. This is a tiny business that still lets him survive.

phrases.english: And Rav said:
selling water
in the valley of Aravot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a term in the ברייתא quoted in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'small store' allowed to a מוחרם is something like selling water in the dry valley of ערבות.

steps.title: A מנודה may learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that a מנודה may learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from Step 29: yes, a מנודה may learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a מנודה may teach and be taught. That settles it: a מנודה is different from an אבל, who may not learn Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: 'learn from it', the question is settled

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not learn Torah, but a מנודה may. Even a מוחרם may learn by himself so he does not forget.

phrases.english: Learn from it.
phrases.notes: This answers the question in Step 29: a מנודה is allowed to learn Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question opened in Step 29, based on the ברייתא in Steps 30-31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מנודה is allowed to learn Torah.

steps.title: May a מצורע learn Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע is allowed to learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of a leper regarding words of Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: may a מצורע speak words of Torah?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the pattern of the whole amud: for each practice of an אבל, the גמרא asks first about a מנודה and then about a מצורע. Now that the מנודה is settled, it asks about the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with צרעת, a spiritual skin disease

phrases.english: A leper, what is [the law]
regarding words of Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the law for a מנודה, the גמרא asks the same question about a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע is allowed to learn Torah.

steps.title: Torah must be learned with awe like at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: from the פסוק linking Torah teaching to the day at חורב, we learn that Torah must be learned with awe, fear, trembling and shaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children, the day you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב.' Just as there it was with dread, fear, trembling and shaking, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer with a ברייתא that sets up a rule: Torah learning must feel like standing at הר סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects teaching Torah to our children with the day at חורב. So learning Torah in every generation must happen with the same awe and fear as at מתן תורה. This rule is the key for the next step, which says who may learn.

keyTerms.meaning: חורב, another name for הר סיני

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children.
The day that you stood
before ה׳ your God at Horeb"
Just as there
it was with dread and with fear
and with trembling and with shaking,
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say the ending out loud: so too here, Torah must be learned with that same awe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question about a מצורע by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sets up the rule that Torah must be learned with awe, which decides who may learn.

steps.title: Who may and may not learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: From this rule the ברייתא says זבין, מצורעין and בועלי נדות may learn all parts of Torah, but בעלי קריין may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: זבין, מצורעין and those who had relations with a נדה may read תורה, נביאים and כתובים, and learn מדרש, תלמוד, הלכות and אגדות. But בעלי קריין, those who had a seminal emission, are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the 'awe' rule and lists who may learn Torah and who may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even people with very strong טומאה, like a זב or a מצורע, may learn every part of Torah. Only a בעל קרי is forbidden. The usual explanation is that his state comes from lightheadedness, which clashes with the awe needed for Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: men who are טמא from a זיבה discharge
men who had relations with a נדה
men who had a seminal emission
learning that draws laws out of the פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that טומאה itself stops a person from learning Torah. The very טמא ones (זב, מצורע) are allowed. The only one forbidden is the בעל קרי, and the reason is tied to the awe rule, not to how strong the טומאה is.

phrases.english: From here they said:
zavim and lepers
and those who had relations with menstruating women
are permitted to read the Torah
and the Prophets and the Writings,
and to learn midrash and Talmud,
halachos and aggados.
But those who had a seminal emission are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the awe rule from Step 35 to list who may learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זבין, מצורעין and בועלי נדות may learn all of Torah; בעלי קריין may not.

steps.title: A מצורע may learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a מצורע may learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from Step 34: a מצורע is allowed to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed מצורעין among those allowed to learn. So even though a מצורע is strict like a מנודה in other ways, Torah learning stays open to him.
steps.whatToRemember: A מנודה and a מצורע may both learn Torah. An אבל may not.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the answer to Step 34 from the ברייתא in Steps 35-36.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מצורע is allowed to learn Torah.

steps.title: An אבל may not launder clothes
steps.stepSummary: A new law: an אבל may not launder his clothes, learned from the פסוק where יואב tells the wise woman of תקוע to act like a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is forbidden to launder, as it says: 'And יואב sent to תקוע and took from there a wise woman, and said to her: Please act as a mourner, and put on mourning clothes, and do not anoint yourself with oil, and be like a woman who has mourned for the dead many days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new law about an אבל: he may not wash his clothes. It brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יואב wanted the woman to look like a real mourner. So he told her to wear mourning clothes, worn like someone who has mourned many days. This picture of an אבל in unwashed mourning clothes is the source that an אבל may not launder.

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden to launder,
as it is written:
"And Yoav sent to Tekoa
and took from there a wise woman
and said to her:
Please act as a mourner
and please put on mourning clothes
and do not anoint yourself with oil
and be like a woman who for many days now
has been mourning for the dead."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the laws of an אבל after finishing the מנודה and מצורע questions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not launder his clothes, learned from the פסוק about the wise woman of תקוע.

steps.title: May ostracized people and lepers launder their clothes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether מנודין and מצורעין are forbidden to launder their clothes, like an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for people in נידוי and for מצורעים about laundering clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just learned that an אבל may not launder. Now it asks whether a מנודה and a מצורע have the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps compared the מנודה and the מצורע to an אבל in other areas. Laundering is a new item, so the גמרא checks whether the comparison holds here too.

keyTerms.meaning: People placed under נידוי (ostracism) by בית דין
People with צרעת (the biblical skin affliction)

phrases.english: Ostracized people and lepers
what is their law regarding laundering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the new אבל rule about laundering and asks whether it also applies to a מנודה and a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מנודין and מצורעין are forbidden to launder.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids them to cut hair and launder
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that מנודין and מצורעין may not cut their hair or launder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: מנודין and מצורעין are forbidden to cut their hair and to launder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא directly says laundering is forbidden for both. It also mentions haircutting, which shows that both rules go together for these people.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Ostracized people and lepers
are forbidden to cut hair and to launder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא says they are forbidden to launder.

steps.title: Conclusion: they may not launder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the ברייתא as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that they may not launder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question: the ברייתא proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא is clear, nothing further is needed. Both a מנודה and a מצורע may not launder.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the proof is accepted

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the ברייתא from step 40.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מנודין and מצורעין are forbidden to launder.

steps.title: A mourner must tear his clothes
steps.stepSummary: An אבל must perform קריעה. We learn this because the sons of אהרן were specially told not to tear, which implies everyone else must.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אבל is obligated to tear his clothes. The Torah told the sons of אהרן "do not tear," which shows that everyone else is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new mourning law, קריעה, along with its source. This sets up the next questions about the מנודה and the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by inference. If the sons of אהרן needed a special command not to tear, then tearing must be the normal rule for every other mourner.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's garment as a sign of mourning

phrases.english: A mourner is obligated to tear his clothes,
since the Merciful One says to the sons of Aaron:
"Do not tear" your clothes,
which implies that everyone else is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from laundering to a new mourning practice, tearing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל must tear his clothes, learned by inference from the command to the sons of אהרן.

steps.title: Must an ostracized person tear his clothes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה is obligated in קריעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of a מנודה regarding tearing his clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks whether the tearing rule for an אבל also applies to a מנודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנודה has already been compared to an אבל in several areas, including laundering. The question is whether tearing is also part of that comparison.

phrases.english: What is the law of an ostracized person regarding tearing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the tearing rule of step 42 to a מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה must tear his clothes.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question about the מנודה is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot find a source, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. The question of whether a מנודה must tear remains undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is "no." It only means the גמרא could not prove either side.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends step 43 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a מנודה must tear is unresolved.

steps.title: Must a leper tear his clothes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע is obligated in קריעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of a מצורע regarding tearing his clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same tearing question, this time about a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After failing to answer for the מנודה, the גמרא tries the מצורע. Here a source may exist, since the Torah describes how a מצורע must dress.

phrases.english: What is the law of a leper regarding tearing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as step 43, now about a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע must tear his clothes.

steps.title: The פסוק says a leper's clothes are torn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that "בגדיו יהיו פרומים" means his clothes must be torn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "His garments shall be פרומים" means that they must be torn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that explains the פסוק about the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads פרומים as "torn." So the Torah itself requires a מצורע's clothes to be torn.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"His garments shall be rent"
meaning that they shall be torn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires a מצורע's clothes to be torn.

steps.title: Conclusion: a leper must tear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: a מצורע tears his clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that a מצורע must tear his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question with a clear answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the מנודה, the מצורע has a direct פסוק. So he is obligated in קריעה.
steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not launder and must tear. The מנודה and the מצורע also may not launder. The מצורע must tear, but for the מנודה tearing is unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 46.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מצורע is obligated to tear his clothes.

steps.title: A mourner must overturn his bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states a new rule: an אבל is obligated in כפיית המטה. It then introduces a teaching of בר קפרא as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is obligated to overturn his bed, as בר קפרא taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a new rule: an אבל must turn his bed over. It then sets up the next move by saying a source from בר קפרא is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh topic. Until now the גמרא was asking about a מנודה and a מצורע, and now it states a rule about the אבל himself. The word דתני tells us the proof is a ברייתא taught by בר קפרא, and its wording comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner, someone who has lost a close relative
Overturning the bed, turning it upside down

phrases.english: A mourner is obligated to overturn the bed,
as בר קפרא taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבֵל חַיָּיב בִּכְפִיַּית הַמִּטָּה, דְּתָנֵי בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the questions about the מנודה and the מצורע end, the גמרא moves to a new obligation of the אבל and introduces its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל is obligated in כפיית המטה. The source is a ברייתא of בר קפרא, which comes next.
